etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French intellectuel, from Latin intellectualis.

definitions.definition: Pertaining to, or performed by, the intellect; mental or cognitive.

quote.citation: 1920, Harold Monro, Preface to s:The year's at the spring; an anthology of recent poetry
quote.text: Pleasure is various, but it cannot exist where the emotions or the imagination have not been powerfully stirred. Whether it be called sensual or intellectual, pleasure cannot be willed

definitions.definition: Endowed with intellect; having a keen sense of understanding; having the capacity for higher forms of knowledge or thought; characterized by intelligence or cleverness

quote.citation: 1894, Edgar Wilson Nye, “Chapter 30”, in Nye's History of the USA:
quote.text: The Fenimore Cooper Indian is no doubt a brave and highly intellectual person, educated abroad, refined and cultivated by foreign travel, graceful in the grub dance or scalp walk-around, yet tender-hearted as a girl, walking by night fifty-seven miles in a single evening to warn his white friends of danger.

definitions.definition: Suitable for exercising one's intellect; perceived by the intellect

quote.citation: 1916, Joseph McCabe, “Chapter IX”, in The Tyranny of Shams:
quote.text: A good deal of nonsense is written about sport and entertainment. Many of us can, with pleasant ease, suspend a severely intellectual task for a few hours to witness a first-class football match.

definitions.definition: Relating to the understanding; treating of the mind.

quote.citation: 1805, William Wordsworth, The Prelude, Book II, lines 331-334 (eds. Jonathan Wordsworth, M. H. Abrams, & Stephen Gill, published by W. W. Norton & Company, 1979):
quote.text: I deem not profitless those fleeting moods / Of shadowy exultation; not for this, / That they are kindred to our purer mind / And intellectual life  […]

definitions.definition: An intelligent, learned person, especially one who discourses about learned matters.

quote.citation: 1941, George Orwell, The Lion and the Unicorn:
quote.text: It should be noted that there is now no intelligentsia that is not in some sense "Left". Perhaps the last right-wing intellectual was T. E. Lawrence. Since about 1930 everyone describable as an “intellectual” has lived in a state of chronic discontent with the existing order.

quote.citation: 1991 September, Stephen Fry, chapter 1, in The Liar, London: Heinemann, →ISBN, →OCLC, section I, page 14:
quote.text: ‘You know I hate intellectuals.’‘You mean you hate people who are cleverer than you are.’‘Yes. I suppose that’s why I like you so much, Tom.’

definitions.definition: (archaic) The intellect or understanding; mental powers or faculties.

quote.citation: 1646, Thomas Browne, chapter 1, in Pseudodoxia Epidemica: […], London:  […]  T[homas] H[arper] for Edward Dod, […], →OCLC, 1st book, page 2:
quote.text: […]  although their intellectuals had not failed in the theory of truth, yet did the inservient and brutall faculties control the suggestion of reason  […]
